page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.large is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2067.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.49 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 2086.47 and the Passmark memory score of 866.04 both fall into the bottom tier. Large-block memory read and write bandwidths are also low, measuring 13.13 GB/sec and 14.34 GB/sec respectively.

The c7i-flex.large offers an entry-level compute-optimized profile with high single-thread execution speeds, but it is constrained by its dual-vCPU limit and low memory bandwidth. This makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require modern Intel instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and AMX, without demanding high parallel processing power or large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include light single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and small-scale text processing, whereas database operations and multi-threaded compilation are limited by the hardware's resource density.
